body.statement: Let a deterministic finite population of uniformly bounded vector attributes be partitioned by complete randomization into a fixed number \(Q\) of groups whose limiting proportions are strictly positive.  If the finite-population covariance matrices converge and the largest squared centered attribute is negligible relative to the total quadratic variation in every nondegenerate projection, then every fixed linear contrast of the group means converges, after normalization by its randomization covariance, to a centered Gaussian law.  The multivariate conclusion follows by the Cram\'{e}r--Wold device.
